comparisons.peer_topic: Investment Banking Fee Performance and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Total Corporation investment banking fees increased 31 percent to $6.2 billion compared to the same period in 2023, primarily driven by higher debt and equity issuance fees and higher advisory fees.
comparisons.comparison: Both Morgan Stanley and Bank of America reported significant year-over-year growth in investment banking revenues driven by similar mix of activities. Morgan Stanley reported a 35% increase to $6.17 billion, attributing growth to higher M&A advisory, equity underwriting (IPOs/follow-ons), and fixed income underwriting. Similarly, Bank of America reported a 31% increase to $6.2 billion, driven by higher debt and equity issuance fees and higher advisory fees. Both firms highlight advisory fees and equity/debt underwriting as the primary growth vectors.

sentences.text: Net revenues of $6,170 million in 2024 increased 35% compared with the prior year, reflecting an increase in underwriting and Advisory revenues.
• Advisory revenues increased primarily due to higher completed M&A transactions.
• Equity underwriting revenues increased primarily on higher initial public offerings and follow-on offerings.
• Fixed income underwriting revenues increased primarily reflecting higher bond issuances, non-investment grade loan issuances and securitized products revenues.

Total Corporation investment banking fees, which exclude self-led deals and are primarily included within Global Banking and Global Markets, increased 31 percent to $6.2 billion compared to the same period in 2023 primarily due to higher debt and equity issuance fees and higher advisory fees.

comparisons.peer_summary: Investment Banking revenues increased 38%, fueled by a 42% rise in fees from rebounding wallet activity and gains across products, including a 61% increase in DCM underwriting fees due to record debt issuance and a 38% increase in equity underwriting fees from stronger follow-on and convertibles activity.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and Morgan Stanley both reported strong double-digit percentage growth in investment banking revenues for 2024, fueled by similar drivers. Citigroup saw a 38% increase, noting specific gains in DCM underwriting (61% increase) due to record debt issuance and equity underwriting (38% increase) from follow-ons. Morgan Stanley reported a 35% increase, also driven by higher bond issuances (fixed income) and equity underwriting from IPOs and follow-ons. Both disclosures emphasize the recovery in underwriting activity across debt and equity products.

sentences.text: Net revenues of $6,170 million in 2024 increased 35% compared with the prior year, reflecting an increase in underwriting and Advisory revenues.
• Equity underwriting revenues increased primarily on higher initial public offerings and follow-on offerings.
• Fixed income underwriting revenues increased primarily reflecting higher bond issuances, non-investment grade loan issuances and securitized products revenues.
Investment Banking revenues increased 38%, reflecting a 42% increase in investment banking fees, due to a rebound in overall wallet activity and wallet share gains across all products.
DCM underwriting fees increased 61%, benefiting from near record debt issuance, particularly in investment grade and higher leveraged finance activity.
Equity underwriting fees increased 38%, due to stronger follow-on and convertibles activity.

comparisons.peer_summary: Investment banking revenues were $7.74 billion in 2024, up 24% from 2023, primarily due to significantly higher revenues in debt underwriting (leveraged finance) and equity underwriting (secondary and IPOs), as well as higher advisory revenues from increased M&A activity.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley both highlighted significant growth in investment banking revenues driven by a recovery in underwriting and advisory. Goldman Sachs reported a 24% increase to $7.74 billion, primarily due to higher debt underwriting (leveraged finance) and equity underwriting (secondary/IPOs), as well as higher advisory revenues from increased M&A. Morgan Stanley reported a 35% increase, also driven by higher completed M&A transactions (advisory) and increased equity/fixed income underwriting. Both firms identify M&A advisory and debt/equity underwriting as the key growth drivers for the year.

sentences.text: Net revenues of $6,170 million in 2024 increased 35% compared with the prior year, reflecting an increase in underwriting and Advisory revenues.
• Advisory revenues increased primarily due to higher completed M&A transactions.
• Equity underwriting revenues increased primarily on higher initial public offerings and follow-on offerings.
• Fixed income underwriting revenues increased primarily reflecting higher bond issuances, non-investment grade loan issuances and securitized products revenues.

Investment banking revenues in the consolidated statements of earnings were $7.74 billion for 2024, 24% higher than 2023, primarily reflecting significantly higher revenues in debt underwriting, primarily driven by leveraged finance activity, and in equity underwriting, primarily driven by secondary and initial public offerings.
In addition, revenues in advisory were higher, reflecting an increase in completed mergers and acquisitions transactions.

comparisons.peer_summary: Investment banking fees increased in 2024 due to favorable market conditions, resulting in higher debt underwriting fees from increased leveraged loans and bond issuances, higher equity underwriting fees from IPO and follow-on offerings, and higher advisory fees from increased M&A activity.
comparisons.comparison: JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley both attribute their investment banking revenue growth to favorable market conditions resulting in higher fees across advisory and underwriting. JPMorgan noted increases in debt underwriting (leveraged loans/bonds), equity underwriting (IPOs/follow-ons), and advisory (M&A). Morgan Stanley similarly reported growth driven by higher M&A advisory, equity underwriting (IPOs/follow-ons), and fixed income underwriting (bond/loan issuances). Both disclosures reflect a broad-based recovery in deal flow across the major investment banking segments.

sentences.text: Net revenues of $6,170 million in 2024 increased 35% compared with the prior year, reflecting an increase in underwriting and Advisory revenues.
• Advisory revenues increased primarily due to higher completed M&A transactions.
• Equity underwriting revenues increased primarily on higher initial public offerings and follow-on offerings.
• Fixed income underwriting revenues increased primarily reflecting higher bond issuances, non-investment grade loan issuances and securitized products revenues.
Investment banking fees increased, reflecting in CIB the benefit of favorable market conditions, which resulted in:
• higher debt underwriting fees predominantly driven by higher industry-wide issuances in leveraged loans, and in high-grade and high-yield bonds,
• higher equity underwriting fees driven by higher industry-wide fees and wallet share gains in IPOs, and in follow-on and convertible securities offerings, and
• higher advisory fees driven by higher industry-wide mergers and acquisitions ("M&A") activity and wallet share gains.
